text: Ah, there you are! I knew our new franchise owner would be here soon. What should I call you?
Let’s get your picture for the league program. Make it look like you.
Every owner comes from somewhere. Where are you from, and what did you do before this?
The top franchises aren’t for sale. These four clubs finished at the bottom of the league and need an owner willing to rebuild. Pick your opportunity.
How hard do you want this league to be? Choose carefully: it is set for the life of your franchise, and the Hall of Fame judges you by it.
Last thing: three monsters have agreed to lead a rebuild. Any position, any element, pick the one you want to build around. Your first week starts Monday.
Team colors follow the club you pick next. You can change your look any time from My office.
⚔️ Your division rival: {rival} · new GM {rivalGms}. You meet twice a season.
You meet twice a season, home and away. Rivalry results are tracked for your whole career.
Locked once the franchise starts. Game length and coaching mode can still be changed in Settings.
Not what you had in mind?
A balanced coaching staff is hired for you. You can replace anyone later from the Staff screen.
Please enter your first and last name.
His Temper (how efficiently he trains each attribute) is drawn when he signs.
Your new franchise could not be saved ({message}). {f}Free some space and try again.
{text} Change it any time in Settings or from ? Help.
Focus strength. Passing {passing} · Rushing {rushing} · Coverage {coverage} · Pass rush {passrush}
Classic natural grass. No type is favored.
Frost-glazed turf, snowbanks along the sidelines.
Dark scorched turf, glowing vents beyond the end lines.
Deep natural grass ringed by old trees.
Under a permanent thunderhead; lightning rods line the stands.
Packed sand and red rock. White lines, hard footing.
A sealed steel dome on synthetic turf. No weather, ever.
Blue-green turf with wave markings; tide pools along the sidelines.
Sun-gold turf, white-and-gold trim, lanterns down both sidelines.
Deep purple turf under low mist. The lines stay bright.
Ancient stone, crimson and purple banners, dragon statues on guard. A look only: no type is favored.
Lives for drama. Has never once let a quote go.
Treats every monster incident as a matter of record.
First season on the beat. Still finding the stadium.
Coach, somebody in the {opp} building says your club is "a bye week with uniforms". Care to respond?
I don’t respond to anonymous quotes. We’ll play the game Sunday.
Tell "somebody" to say it on the fifty-yard line. We’ll be there at kickoff.
A bye week with uniforms still shows up better dressed than their defense.
I AM the bye week. I am rest. I am inevitable. Next question.
Is it true you and the {opp} coach don’t shake hands, or did I make that up to get a quote?
We have a professional relationship and I respect their staff.
I’ll shake their hand after the game. It’ll be the only thing they catch all day.
You made it up. But it’s a good rumor, so I’m keeping it.
We don’t shake hands. We headbutt. It’s in the bylaws.
Scale of one to ten, how overrated are the {opp}?
They’re a good club. I’m not putting a number on anybody.
I’d say a strong seven, which is also how many yards I expect them to gain.
Numbers are a prison. I rate them "purple".
Which club in this league would you least like to have dinner with?
I’d sit down with any of them. It’s a league of good people.
The {opp}. They’d fumble the bread basket.
Any club with a Dragon type. I’ve seen what they do to a buffet.
I only dine alone, in the end zone, at midnight.
Give me one word for the {opp}. Just one. Make it a headline.
"Sunday." As in, that’s when we find out.
If you and the {opp} coach raced forty yards, who wins and how badly?
I’d rather settle things with the teams on the field.
Me. They’d pull a hamstring reading the starting line.
Neither. We’d both be carted off by the fifteen.
I would simply become the wind.
Be honest: is there a coach in this league you just can’t stand?
No. Competing hard isn’t the same as disliking someone.
There’s a list. The {opp} just moved up it.
Yes. Me, during the fourth quarter.
The one who lives in my mirror. He knows what he did.
Guarantee a win on Sunday. Go on. Do it. Right into this microphone.
I guarantee effort and preparation. The scoreboard takes care of itself.
Guaranteed. Write it in pen. Write it on the {opp} bus.
I guarantee somebody wins. I’m very confident in that.
I guarantee the sun will rise and it will be afraid of us.
Your fans are calling the {opp} mascot "a rug with opinions". Do you condone that?
We ask our fans to keep it respectful to everyone.
I condone it. I may have started it.
I’d never say that. Rugs have a purpose.
The rug and I have spoken. We have an understanding.
Who’s the most dangerous monster in this league that ISN’T on your roster? Careful, they’re listening.
There’s talent on every club. I won’t single anyone out.
Nobody. If they were that dangerous they’d play for us.
The vending machine at our facility. It’s taken more money than free agency.
The moon. Nobody game-plans for the moon.
Is {star} the best monster in this league, or just the best one you could afford?
He’s as good as anyone, and he makes everyone around him better.
Best in the league. Ask anyone who’s had to tackle him.
Both. Mostly the second. Please don’t tell him.
{star} is not a monster. {star} is a season.
Coach, a league study suggests Fire types are responsible for most sideline heater malfunctions. Does your club have a protocol?
We follow every league safety guideline.
Our protocol is scoring so much that nobody’s cold.
Yes. We stand slightly further away and hope.
The heaters work for us now. They’ve chosen a side.
From a schematic standpoint, how do you account for an opponent who can, hypothetically, fly?
Leverage and discipline. Fundamentals don’t change.
Let them fly. The ball still has to come down, and we’ll be under it.
We’ve asked the league to enforce gravity more consistently.
We have a net. A very big net. I’ve said too much.
Hydration is critical. In general terms, how does a staff manage a Water type who IS the hydration?
Our trainers have individual plans for everyone.
We don’t manage it. We aim it at the other sideline.
He is not hydrated. We are all hydrated THROUGH him.
Analytics say going for it on fourth down is correct far more often than coaches do it. Why the hesitation across the league?
Every situation is different. We weigh field position, the clock and the matchup.
Other coaches are scared. I’m not other coaches.
Because analytics has never been yelled at by an owner.
I go for it on first down. It confuses everyone, including us.
What is the single most important measurable when you evaluate a monster? Please be specific.
Awareness. A monster who knows where to be makes everyone better.
Whether the other club is afraid of him.
Whether he fits through the locker room door.
There is a theory that Ice types perform worse in warm stadiums. Does the data in your building support it?
We prepare our monsters to play anywhere.
Our Ice types make the stadium cold. That’s the data.
The only data I have is a puddle where a linebacker used to be.
Temperature is a rumor started by thermometers.
Clock management: walk me through your decision tree with ninety seconds and two timeouts.
We’ve rehearsed it. Sideline first, then the middle, save one for the kick.
My decision tree is: we’re already winning.
It’s less of a tree and more of a nervous shrub.
I throw the clock into the crowd. No clock, no problem.
Is roster chemistry quantifiable, in your professional opinion?
Not fully, but you can see it on tape when two monsters trust each other.
Sure. Count the points we score. That’s the chemistry.
Yes. Ours is currently "two of them share snacks".
I measured it once. The instrument burst into song.
Rule question: if a Psychic type knows the play call before the snap, should that be a penalty?
That’s for the league office. We play by the rules as written.
If they know the call and still can’t stop it, that’s their problem.
Only if he tells the other team. Then it’s just rude.
I’ve started calling plays I haven’t thought of yet. Checkmate.
Looking at the {opp}: what is the key matchup on Sunday, in purely technical terms?
The line of scrimmage. Win there and everything else follows.
Our best against their best. I like ours. A lot.
Me against my own play sheet. It’s laminated and I still lose it.
My left hand against my right. Only one calls plays.
Which single trait of {star}’s translates most directly into wins for this club?
His preparation. He’s the same every day, and the others follow it.
The one where he’s better than whoever the {opp} put across from him.
His ability to make my play calls look intentional.
His aura. We had it measured. The device is still humming.
Coach, if you score more points than the {opp}, does that improve your chances of winning?
It does. That’s the plan every week.
It guarantees it. Tell the {opp} I said so.
Significantly. We ran the numbers twice.
Points are a state of mind. But yes.
How many quarters are you planning to play on Sunday?
All four, and we’ll be ready for overtime.
Four. The {opp} usually stop after two.
We’re aiming for four. Five felt greedy.
As many as it takes. I have brought extra quarters.
Is the football the same one you used last week, or do you get a new one?
The league supplies new game balls each week.
We wear ours out. Too many touchdowns.
Same one. We’re very attached to it. His name is Gerald.
There has only ever been one football. Think about it.
Which is more important, offense or defense? My editor said to ask.
Both. You need all three phases to win.
Whichever one is on the field when the {opp} are crying.
Parking. Have you seen our lot on game day?
Do the monsters know the rules, or do you just tell them where to run?
They know the rules. They study as hard as any athlete.
They know one rule: don’t let the other team have nice things.
About sixty percent of them. It’s a strong sixty.
I don’t tell them anything. They tell me. I’m a hostage.
What’s your favorite play? Is it the one where you get the points?
Any play that’s executed the way we practiced it.
The one where the {opp} coach throws his headset.
Kneeling at the end. It means we got away with it.
The one where everybody runs left and I run home.
When you say "we need to execute", who is being executed? Is everyone okay?
It just means doing your job on each play. Everyone’s fine.
The other team’s hopes. Not okay. Thanks for asking.
Nobody is okay. Welcome to football.
Why is it called a "down" if the goal is to go up the field?
It’s an old term for a play. Good question, actually.
Because that’s where the {opp} end up.
Up and down are the same direction if you’re brave enough.
I wrote down "win the turnover battle". Is that a different game you play at halftime?
It means taking the ball away more than you give it up.
It’s the game where we take their ball and keep it.
Yes. It’s held in the parking lot. Bring pastries.
It is an ancient duel. I can say no more.
Sorry, I got lost on the way in. Which one of you is the coach?
That’s me. Take your time, you’re doing fine.
I’m the one the {opp} have nightmares about.
I’m the one who looks tired. Narrow it down from there.
There is no coach. There is only the whistle.
Is {star} your best one? He’s the only one I recognize.
He’s our leader, and he’s earned it. But it takes all of them.
He’s the best one. The {opp} will recognize him too, from behind.
He’s the best one. The others know. We don’t discuss it.
{n} straight wins. Has the rest of the league just given up, or are you that good?
We’re playing well, but every week starts at zero.
I’d say we’re good. The league says we’re "under review".
We are no longer a team. We are a weather system.
At {n} consecutive wins, regression to the mean is a concern. How do you guard against it?
Same preparation, same standards. Streaks don’t change the work.
We are the mean now. Everyone else can regress to us.
I guard against it by not knowing what it means.
The mean came to my office. I ate it.
You’ve won {n} in a row! Do you get a prize, or do you have to keep going?
No prize yet. We keep going until the season’s over.
The prize is everybody else’s tears.
We get a coupon. One free loss. Trying not to use it.
The prize is more football. It’s a curse, really.
{n} straight losses. Who’s to blame? I need a name and I need it spelled correctly.
It starts with me. We’ll fix it together.
Blame the schedule. And the refs. And whoever’s holding that microphone.
Blame is a river. I am but a duck upon it.
After {n} consecutive losses, at what point does rebuilding become an archaeological excavation?
We’re not rebuilding. We’re correcting, one week at a time.
Keep digging. You’ll find the win we’re about to bury the {opp} under.
We’ve found some pottery and a very old playbook.
We dug so deep we found a second, worse team.
You’ve lost {n} in a row. Have you tried winning instead?
That’s the goal. We’re working on it every day.
We’re saving it for the {opp}. Surprise.
We tried it once. Didn’t care for the attention.
Winning is just losing in a nicer hat.
It’s {rival} week. {rivalGm} says your defense couldn’t stop a shopping cart. Is that accurate?
It’s a big game for both clubs. We’ll let our play answer.
Tell {rivalGm} the cart’s coming Sunday, and it’s full of touchdowns.
Depends on the cart. Is it one with the wobbly wheel?
We stopped a shopping cart once. It never recovered. Neither did we.
Any message for {rivalGm} and {rival} before Sunday? I’ll deliver it personally. Loudly.
Respect. We’re looking forward to a good game.
They should be worried. We’re coming, and we’re bringing snacks for after.
Tell them we said hi. Then run.
Tell {rivalGm} the owl knows. That’s all. He’ll understand.
Historically, rivalry games are decided by emotional regulation. How regulated is your club ahead of {rival}?
We’re focused. It’s a big game, and we’re treating it like the next one.
We did breathing exercises. A linebacker hyperventilated.
I have regulated nothing since the preseason.
Why don’t you and {rival} like each other? Did they take your parking spot?
It’s a rivalry. Two good clubs that want the same thing.
They took our spot, our lunch and soon an L.
It was the parking spot. It’s always the parking spot.
It began long ago, over a sandwich. The sandwich is still out there.
At {record}, you are mathematically in the playoff race. What is your internal projection?
We don’t project. We prepare for the {opp} and count at the end.
Our projection is everybody else staying home.
My internal projection is mostly indigestion.
I asked the numbers. The numbers asked for a lawyer.
You’re {record}. Is that good? People keep saying "the race" and I don’t see anyone running.
It keeps us in contention. Every game matters from here.
It’s good enough to ruin somebody’s December.
We’re running. It’s just very slow and there’s a lot of standing around.
The race is inside us. Mine has a cramp.
It’s the playoffs. Lose and you’re done. Who on the {opp} are you sending home personally?
Nobody personally. We respect how hard it is to get here.
All of them. I’ve booked the bus.
Their kicker. He looks like he has plans anyway.
I will send them home one at a time, by catapult.
Is a playoff game longer than a normal game, or does it just feel like it?
Same length. The stakes are what make it feel different.
For the {opp} it’ll feel like forever.
It’s the same, but everyone forgets how to breathe.
Time stops in the playoffs. I’ve been here since last year.
You’re the defending Beast Bowl champions. Everyone wants your head. Whose head do YOU want?
Nobody’s. Last season is over. We’re earning it again.
I’ve got the trophy. They can have the envy.
I just want my own head back. The parade was a lot.
I collect helmets now. Don’t ask what’s in them.
You won the Beast Bowl! Do you have to give the trophy back if you lose on Sunday?
No, it’s ours to keep. But we want another one.
No. And the {opp} aren’t getting near it.
No, but they do make you dust it.
The trophy and I are legally married.
{name} threw {ints} interceptions against {lastOpp}. Has your quarterback considered throwing to his own team?
He knows he has to be better. We’ve looked at every one of them on tape.
He was being generous. That ends Sunday.
We’ve color-coded the jerseys for him. Fingers crossed.
He wasn’t throwing interceptions. He was making friends.
{ints} interceptions for {name} last week. Is this a decision-making issue or a mechanical one?
A bit of both. We’ve addressed it and I expect a cleaner game.
It’s a "their defense got lucky" issue.
It’s mechanical. The mechanism is his arm, and it’s pointing the wrong way.
It is a spiritual issue. The ball has lost faith in him.
When {name} threw it to the other team {ints} times, was that part of a trick play?
No. Those were mistakes, and he owns them.
Yes. The trick is we win anyway.
A very long trick. We’re still waiting for the reveal.
The trick is on all of us.
{name} threw {tds} touchdown passes against {lastOpp}. Is that sustainable, statistically?
He’s seeing it well. We’ll keep giving him clean looks.
No. I’ve asked him to pace himself so I look less replaceable.
He has seen the future, and it is in the end zone.
{name} ran for {yds} yards against {lastOpp}. Is your running back legally classified as a natural disaster?
He ran hard and the line gave him lanes. Credit all of them.
The paperwork’s pending. The {opp} should evacuate.
Not yet, but the insurance people have called twice.
He is classified as "inevitable". The league agreed quickly.
{name} got {yds} yards last week. Is that a lot? How many yards are there?
It’s an excellent day for a back. He earned every one.
It’s more than the {opp} will get as a team.
There are a hundred. He used most of them, some twice.
There are infinite yards. He has merely begun.
{name} torched {lastOpp} for {yds} receiving yards. Should the {opp} secondary just stay on the bus?
He had a great day. The {opp} will have a plan for him, and we’ll need answers.
They can stay on the bus. He’ll catch passes over that too.
They should at least keep the engine running.
There is no bus. There is only {name}.
{name} was everywhere against {lastOpp}. How do you quantify that kind of defensive performance?
Effort and film study. He’s earned everything he’s getting.
You count the quarterbacks who ask to go home.
We count the number of times the other coach says "who is that?"
You cannot quantify a thunderstorm. You can only apologize to it.
{name} is out for {weeks}. What is the adjustment at {pos}, structurally?
Next monster up. We adjust the plan around who we have.
The adjustment is we’re still better than the {opp}.
Structurally, we’re holding it together with tape and optimism.
I have replaced him with a very convincing shrub.
With {name} hurt, do you play with one fewer monster, or are you allowed a spare?
We have depth for exactly this. Somebody steps in.
We could play with one fewer and still beat the {opp}.
We’re allowed a spare. He’s been in the trunk all season.
We all become {name} now. It’s a team-building thing.
{name} has evolved and appears considerably larger. Has the league approved this?
It’s a natural part of his development. Everything’s by the book.
The league can approve it from underneath him.
We filed the form. Under "reason" we wrote "look at him".
The league did not approve. {name} did not ask.
{name} looks different. Did he get a haircut, or is that the evolving thing?
That’s the evolution. He’s worked a long time for it.
That’s the evolving thing. The {opp} get to meet it first.
Both. The barber is still recovering.
He has shed his former self. We keep it in a jar.
You have {name}, an actual legendary, on the roster. Isn’t that basically cheating?
He’s on our roster by the rules, and he works as hard as anyone.
It’s only cheating if we win. So, yes, eventually.
He was here before the rules. The rules live in his shadow.
Is {name} really a legendary? Does he know? Should someone tell him?
He knows. He handles it with a lot of humility.
He knows. So will the {opp}, by the second quarter.
We told him. He asked for a bigger locker.
He has always known. He told ME.
You traded for {name}. Who did you fleece, and do they know yet?
It was a fair deal for both clubs. We’re glad to have him.
They’ll know on Sunday. And every Sunday after.
They know. They sent a thank-you card. It was sarcastic.
I traded a dream I had for him. Best dream I ever sold.
The acquisition of {name}: what need does that trade address in the depth chart?
He gives us quality at {pos} and competition in that room.
It addresses our need to embarrass people at {pos}.
It addresses my need to feel something in the trade window.
He fills the hole. The hole in all of us.
You signed {name}. Walk me through the valuation model that produced that contract.
He fits what we do and the number worked under the cap.
The model is simple: he’s good and now the {opp} don’t have him.
I wrote a number, he nodded, we both pretended it was planned.
The model is a goat that points at things.
You got a new monster, {name}! Did you pick him, or did he come with the building?
We picked him. Our scouts liked him a lot.
We picked him. The {opp} wanted him. Too slow.
He was in the lobby. Nobody asked questions.
He chose us. We do not know why. We are afraid to ask.
Word is the board’s patience is gone. How warm is that seat, Coach? Describe it for the readers.
I’m focused on Sunday. The rest isn’t mine to control.
Warm enough to cook the {opp} on.
Medium-rare. I’ve asked for a cushion.
I no longer sit. I hover. It’s safer.
People keep saying you’re "on the hot seat". Can’t you just ask for a different chair?
It’s a figure of speech. It means I need to win.
I’ll get a new chair after we beat the {opp}. A throne.
I asked. The new chair was also on fire.
All chairs are hot if you sit with enough guilt.
Nobody picked you to beat {lastOpp}, and you won {us}-{them}. Who do you want an apology from first?
Nobody. We just want to stack another good week.
Everyone. Alphabetical order. Starting with you.
My own family. They had {lastOpp} in the office pool.
I want an apology from the concept of doubt.
{lastOpp} beat you {them}-{us}. At what point did you personally stop watching?
I watched every snap. We own that one and we’ve moved on to the {opp}.
I’ve already forgotten it. The {opp} are about to help everyone else forget too.
I’m still watching. It’s playing on the inside of my eyelids.
You lost {them}-{us} to {lastOpp}. Was the plan to let them tire themselves out scoring?
No. We were outplayed, and we’ve worked on why.
Yes. And now they’re exhausted and we’re fresh for the {opp}.
Yes. It nearly worked. They looked very tired at {them}.
There was no plan. There has never been a plan. Shh.
A {us}-{them} win over {lastOpp}. Is there a risk of overconfidence in the building?
There’s always something to clean up. We found plenty on tape.
It isn’t overconfidence if you’re right.
Enormous risk. I’ve already ordered the rings.
We have transcended confidence. We simply know.
Your game with {lastOpp} went to overtime. Is that because nobody was keeping track of the time?
It means the score was level after four quarters.
It’s because {lastOpp} needed extra time to lose properly.
Yes. The clock guy stepped out for a sandwich.
Time gave up on us. We kept playing out of spite.
Before I start: you took a shot at me from that podium a while back. My readers noticed. Anything you’d like to take back?
That was uncalled for. I apologize. Ask your question.
I take back nothing. I’d like to add to it.
I’d take it back, but it got a bigger laugh than our offense.
I said what the prophecy required.
Um. Last time I asked a question you made fun of me, and my mum saw it. Can I still ask one?
Of course. That was on me, and I’m sorry. Go ahead.
You can ask. I can’t promise your mum will like this one either.
Tell your mum I said hello, and that you’re doing great.
Your mother and I have been in correspondence. Proceed.
For the record, your previous remark about my methodology has been noted in my methodology. Shall we proceed?
Understood. I respect the work you do.
Note this one too: I still don’t read your charts.
I am in your footnotes now. I live there.
You stood up here and called it against {lastOpp}, and then you went and did it. Are you insufferable now?
We backed it up. Now it’s the {opp}, and that one’s over.
Insufferable and undefeated in predictions. Want another one?
I was insufferable before. Now I have evidence.
I do not predict. I remember forwards.
You guaranteed big things against {lastOpp} from this very podium. Then you lost {them}-{us}. Would you like the clip played back?
I said it and we didn’t back it up. That’s on me.
Play it. I’ll say it again about the {opp}, and this time I’m right.
No thank you. I’ve seen it. My whole family sent it to me.
That was a different me. He has been dealt with.
{rivalGm} says your trash talk before the {rival} game was "noise" and the win was "luck". Your reply?
We played well that day. I’ll leave it there.
Tell {rivalGm} the noise has a scoreboard attached.
It was luck. We’ve been practicing luck all year.
The noise is coming from inside {rivalGm}’s house.
{rivalGm} had your quotes pinned to the {rival} locker room wall, and then they beat you. Any regrets?
Yes. They earned it, and I gave them the motivation.
No regrets. I’ll write them a new wall next time.
Only that I didn’t charge them for the decorating.
I regret nothing. The wall and I are in talks.
Earlier this season you told this room, and I quote: "{quote}" Would you care to clarify that for the record?
I was having some fun. It’s a long season.
I stand by every word. So should the {opp}.
I’d clarify it, but I think it’s funnier this way.
It clarifies itself, in time, to those who are ready.
My editor made me write down something you said: "{quote}" I’ve read it nine times. What does it mean?
It was a joke. Don’t lose sleep over it.
It means the {opp} are in trouble.
Nobody knows. It was on a mug in my office.
Read it a tenth time. Then come find me.
You talk about {name} at basically every press conference. Is he your favorite? Are coaches allowed favorites?
I’m proud of the whole roster. He’s earned the attention.
I don’t have favorites. I have {name}, and then the others.
I am not allowed to say. {name} is listening.
The {name} fan club wants to know: is it true the other monsters are jealous of all the coverage he gets from this podium?
Not at all. That locker room pulls for each other.
They should be jealous. They should also block better.
One of them asked for "at least a mention". So: hello, the others.
There are no other monsters. There never were.

text: The clock does not tick on its own: each play uses a few seconds, and if the last play ended with the clock running (tackled in bounds, no score), the time between plays comes off when you snap: {normal} s at normal tempo, {hurry} s in hurry-up, {milk} s milking it. The line under the score tells you which. An incompletion, a run out of bounds, a score or a timeout stops it: the next snap then costs nothing.

area: Match day (pregame, play calling, replays, box score)

text: Timeout (three a half) stops the clock so your next snap costs no time, on defense it is how you get the ball back from a team running the clock out. Hurry-up tempo cuts the runoff to {hurry} s for free; milk clock raises it to {milk} s when you are protecting a lead. Spike stops the clock for the price of a down (appears under a minute); kneel burns time when you are ahead, if the other side has no timeouts and less than {milk2} s is left, the clock runs out and the game is over.

text: Watch every exchange. Your monsters enter in the order you set.
The same battle, resolved instantly. Skipping never changes who wins.

Beast Clash is a monster battle. Each side lines up its monsters in an order of entry. One active fighter per side trades strikes; the reserves wait and act only through abilities that name them (a reserve relay, a rescue, a commanded strike). When the active monster is knocked out, the next in line steps up with the battle as it stands (health, shields and statuses carry on). The last side standing wins, or the side with more health left after 30 exchanges.

Rotations. After both fighters have acted, a side may rotate its active monster out for a reserve (at most once every four exchanges). In Watch battle you are asked at each legal rotation: Stay in, bring in a reserve, or Auto for the rest of this battle (the game's own rotation policy, the one the other side uses). A monster that rotates in by choice acts at half strength on its first turn. Knockout replacements and forced rotations carry no penalty.

Watch battle shows every exchange at the speed you choose and asks you about rotations. Skip to results plays the battle instantly with the automatic rotation policy on your side. Neither is a worse chance of winning: a Watch battle in which you choose Auto at the first prompt is the very same battle as Skip.

Statuses. A monster carries one shared status at a time (Shielded, Guarded, Empowered, Weakened, Slowed, Stunned, Confused ...). In the pregame Clash and the overtime Clash, statuses carry into and out of the football game; a standalone Tuesday battle clears them at its end.

Tuesday encounters: the monster you chose fights beside two wild companions. They are matched to your club's strength and cannot be signed; only the monster you chose can join you.
Skipping a Tuesday encounter is different: no battle happens, so there is no chance to sign that monster this week. Nothing else is lost.

Coach’s last prediction still being fact-checked by the scoreboard.
Called the {lastOpp} result. Has mentioned it eleven times since.
Losing streak reaches {n}. Morale described as "technically present".
Winning streak hits {n}. Humility not expected to recover.
Scoreboard operator from the {lastOpp} game still icing wrist.
Nobody saw the {lastOpp} result coming, including {club}.
{us}-{them} rout of {lastOpp} has club "insufferable", neighbors say.
Rivalry game Sunday. Local hospitals request everyone calm down.
Playoff football Sunday. Nails across the city in danger.
Owner’s box described as "quiet, in a loud way".
{name} ran for {yds} yards last week. Groundskeepers still repairing the field.
{name} had {yds} receiving yards last week. Opposing secondary "resting comfortably".
{name} threw {tds} touchdowns last week and would like you to know.
Newly evolved {name} no longer fits in team photo.
New arrival {name} "still learning where the cafeteria is".
New signing {name} reportedly "happy to be here, wherever here is".
{name} out {weeks}. Trainers "doing their best with the tape they have".
{name} seen nodding slowly in background throughout.
Club sits at {record}. Mathematicians cautiously interested.
Reporters outnumbered answers three to one.
Coach thanked reporters. Reporters unsure what for.
League reminds coaches that microphones are "always on".
One reporter laughed so hard he missed deadline.
Team doctor has asked to "just have a quick chat".
Next week: possibly the same coach.
Well played. Don’t get used to it.
Playoff football. Everything you did in October means nothing now.
One game. Bring your best six plays and nothing else.
Three in a row. I am starting to feel bad for {club}.
Same plan as last time? Please say yes.
Good luck out there. {me} won’t make it easy.
We watched your tape. Interesting choices.
Nothing personal. We need this one as much as you do.
Your {star} is the real deal. We’ll see about the rest.
Let’s make it a clean game.
Welcome to the coast. The tide here comes in slow and leaves nothing behind.
Play your game. Mine has been the same for twenty years.
You came in high and fast last time. The water doesn’t mind.
Patience, coach. Learn it, or lose to it again.
You beat the tide once. Nobody beats it twice by accident.
I made some changes. You will notice.
You carry my badge. Carry it well; I intend to take it back today.
Twenty years of the same tide, and you read it in one afternoon. Keep that badge dry.
Tsunarok will want this one back. So will I.
Bright day for it. We throw the ball and we smile while we do it.
Keep up if you can. Most clubs can’t.
Last time you squinted at the sun all afternoon. Bring sunglasses.
Aurelion is faster than your corners. That hasn’t changed.
You found a way to cloud us up. Clever. We practiced in the rain all week.
Round two. The Lions are rested.
The Dawn Badge in your pocket. It suits you. It would suit my trophy case better.
You didn’t squint once. Fine. The Dawn Badge is yours; wear it where I can see it.
Nobody out-shines the Lions twice. Enjoy the day.
Tempo. Tempo. Tempo. If you blink, we scored.
I run plays faster than your coordinator can read them.
You were a step slow last time. A step is all we need.
Voltarch had fun. He wants more.
You slowed us down. Nobody slows us down twice.
New wrinkles this week. Try to keep up.
You kept up. Nobody keeps up. Take the badge before I change my mind.
Voltarch is sulking. That is the nicest thing I can say about today.
We run the ball. You know that. Knowing it won’t help.
Four yards and a cloud of dust, sixty times.
Your front got pushed around last time. Did you fix it or just hope?
Titanolith asked if you were bringing a bigger line.
You stacked the box. Fine. See what happens when we throw.
The Quake Badge. Took me a while to forgive you for that.
Today we take it back the hard way.
You held the line against the canyon. That earns the Quake Badge and my respect, in that order.
Titanolith wants a rematch. He can wait his turn like everyone else.
You won’t see us coming. That’s rather the point.
Trust nothing you see before the snap.
Last time you kept throwing into Nyxshade. Please, go on.
Fooled once. Shall we try for twice?
Hm. You read us. I have rewritten the whole book since.
The Dusk Badge sits with you. The dusk always returns.
Let’s see if you still see in the dark.
You saw through us. Few do. The Dusk Badge is yours… for now.
Nyxshade will study your tape tonight. I will study it tomorrow.
Up here we don’t make mistakes. We can’t afford the cold.
Discipline wins in the snow. Bring some.
Still running that same cover three? We ate it last time.
Glacivern froze your first read. He will do it again.
You beat us at home. I have not slept well since.
The Frost Badge belongs on this mountain. You know that.
Nothing thaws up here, coach. Not even grudges.
Clean football in the cold. I don’t hand this badge to many. Take it.
Glacivern froze nothing today. I will not sleep well.
We hit. That’s the whole speech.
Aegistron doesn’t lose a matchup. Pick a receiver to sacrifice.
You limped off last time. Did your trainer earn his money this week?
You beat the hammer. Respect. Won’t happen twice.
We forged a few new things.
The Forge Badge. You earned it, and I will take it back fair.
Hit first today, or don’t bother.
You hit first all day. The Forge Badge was built for coaches like that.
Aegistron lost a matchup. Write the date down; it will not happen again.
So you are the one they talk about. Show me.
Aurodrax has never been intercepted on a first read. Try.
Last time was a lesson. This one is a test.
You looked at the dragon and blinked.
Once. You beat the dragon once. The dragon remembers.
I have waited all year for this game.
The Wyrm Badge was never meant to leave this stadium.
Hold it tight. It is coming home.
So you are the one they talk about. Now I know why. The Wyrm Badge is yours.
The dragon remembers every scar. This one he will remember with respect.
Division rivals. Same rebuild, different owners. Let’s see who got it right.
I’ll be honest: I bet the board you would finish below us.
We beat you last time. Everyone in the division noticed.
Still running the same six plays? Good.
You got us once. I have spent every day since thinking about it.
This is the one that matters.
Rivals in the playoffs. Someone’s season ends in the family.
Three straight. My board is asking why they still call this a rivalry.
I would wish you luck, but I like winning.
I hear the Board is counting. So am I. Enjoy the job while it lasts.
Lose today and I’ll send flowers to your office. The next owner can keep them.
Confident: back it up and the other coach remembers; lose and the room is rattled next week.
Respect. It’ll be a good game.
Respectful: a calm word before kickoff.
Enjoy the view from up there. It never lasts for your lot.
Nice start. My scouts say your secondary is held together with tape.
The division runs through us. It always has.
We are coming. The Board will hear about it before you do.
Your schedule gets harder. Ours gets us.
Dead even. One of us is lying to their fans.
Tiebreakers favor the club that wants it. That is us.
Rivalry week. I have cleared my calendar for your excuses.
Sunday. Bring the real playbook this time.
My monsters have been talking about this one since the schedule came out.
Win your first game with a franchise.
One. I keep a tally of every GM’s first win, some take a month, some take a season. Yours is on the books. Noted.
Nobody remembers the first one, {first}. Try to make the next few harder to forget.
Beat your rival club for the first time.
So you took one off us. Enjoy the night. I’ve lost to better clubs than yours and I still have the job.
Here’s a tip, free of charge: the second one is the one that matters. Nobody gets it.
Beat your rival twice in one season without losing to them.
I don’t make calls like this. My staff told me not to. I want you to know that I know, and that next year is a long way off.
Seven left, and every one of them has now watched your tape. I’d call that the price of success, but you already know that.
Hold four of the eight gym badges.
Half the gyms. The last GM who held four badges held them for six seasons before the fifth. I mention it only so you know what the other half costs.
EIGHT OF EIGHT. THE GYMS ARE YOURS.
THE BOARD HAS SEEN THIS TWICE IN THE HISTORY OF THE LEAGUE. IT DOES NOT CONGRATULATE. IT RECORDS.
I’ll be honest with you, {first}: when you sat in my office I gave you three years to get here. This is happening very fast.
The Board will have noticed. The Board notices everything. That is not always good news.
Go unbeaten through a regular season.
Nine and oh. I have the sheet in front of me and I keep reading it.
I won’t say it’s never been done. I will say that nobody who did it was still in the job five years later. The league does not like being embarrassed.
Make the playoffs for the first time.
You’re in. Eight clubs, three rounds, no second chances.
The regular season is over, which means the Board stops reading your record and starts reading the bracket. Different document. Same Board.
Conference champions. I watched the whole thing. I’d like to say I was rooting for the other side, but I was rooting for the other side.
One more. You know what the Beast Bowl does to GMs who lose it? Nothing. That’s the part that eats you.
THE BOARD ACKNOWLEDGES THE {YEAR} BEAST BOWL.
YOU WILL BE ASKED FOR ANOTHER. EVERYONE IS.
THE BOARD HAS OPENED A FILE. IT DOES THIS RARELY.
Have one of your monsters win a league award.
One of yours took a league award. {awardLine}
Every other GM in the league just looked up what you’re paying him. So did his agent. Enjoy the ceremony; the renewal comes after.
Ten career wins. A number nobody puts on a plaque, but it’s the one where I stop expecting a GM to disappear.
Thirty. That’s the Hall of Fame line on Rookie, and a third of the way on All-Star. Either way, you’ve outlasted most of the people who sat where you sit.
Fifty. I pulled the file: four GMs in league history reached fifty with one club. Two of them were fired within two years of it. The Board has a long memory and a short patience.
The other GMs will try to win the next two Beast Bowls just to stop you. I would.
Unlock a legendary monster (three Legend Tracks on one).
THE BOARD WILL BE WATCHING THE {REGION} SCOUTING REPORTS.
Qualify for the Hall of Fame.
THE BOARD HAS REVIEWED YOUR RECORD. YOU ARE ELIGIBLE FOR THE HALL OF FAME.
THE DOOR IS OPEN. YOU MAY WALK THROUGH IT WHENEVER YOU CHOOSE. YOU MAY ALSO KEEP WORKING; THE BOARD HAS NO OPINION ON WHICH. IT HAS NEVER WRITTEN THIS LETTER TO THE SAME NAME TWICE.
Meet the Board’s goal while on the hot seat.
You were one miss from a conversation nobody enjoys. You didn’t miss.
For what it’s worth, and in this office it isn’t worth much, I’d have kept you. The Board would not have asked.
Heard you made a trade. Cute. Half this league hasn’t figured out the phone exists.
Call me sometime. I’ll say no, but I’ll enjoy it.

All seventy-two original families, seen and filed. The league archive has asked for a copy of your Dex.
I told them to ask you nicely.
Discover all 120 Basic families in the Beast Dex.
One hundred and twenty Basic families. Most clubs never look twice at a Basic.
You looked at every one of them. That is how good rosters get built.

Each side lines up its monsters in an order of entry. The two front monsters trade strikes, Supports and bench Disruptors act from the back. Football in one breath: the offense has four tries ("downs") to move the ball 10 yards. Make it and you get four more; reach the far end zone for a touchdown (6 points, plus a 1-point kick). Fail on fourth down and the other team takes over, which is why you usually punt or kick a field goal (3 points) on fourth. You coach, you do not steer: pick one of your six play cards, press Snap, and watch the monsters run it.
Key Moments (recommended) simulates the routine snaps and stops for the big downs. Full Coaching lets you call every play, and takes about twice as long. Change it any time in Settings.

Every play uses a few seconds, and if the last play ended with the clock running, the time between plays comes off when you snap. A timeout stops it; hurry-up is free; a spike stops it for the price of a down. Ahead late? Milk the clock or kneel.
